sentences.text: South Australia’s Independent Commissioner Against Corruption assessed amendments to the ICAC Act and their effects on the public integrity system.
sentences.support:
the changes made to the Act also have 
significant consequences for the entire scheme designed to ensure the integrity of public 
administration

sentences.text: The Commissioner concluded that the changes increased the risk of corruption going undetected and weakened public administration’s ability to address it.
sentences.support:
the 
changes create an increased risk of corruption remaining hidden and undermine the 
ability of public administration to deal with it.

sentences.text: The Commissioner said the amendments narrowed the Commission’s jurisdiction, removed its power to initiate investigations and restricted public reporting.
sentences.support:
The changes made by the amending Act limit the Commission’s jurisdiction, curtail 
its independence

sentences.text: The Commissioner also concluded that more complex reporting requirements were likely to reduce information reported about corruption, misconduct and maladministration.
sentences.section: The changes will mean less conduct is reported
sentences.support:
The new and more complex reporting requirements are likely 
to mean that less information about corruption, misconduct and maladministration is 
reported.

findings.quote:
The changes made by the amending Act limit the Commission’s jurisdiction, curtail 
its independence and reduce its ability to effectively identify, deal with and prevent 
corruption in public administration.

The new and more complex reporting requirements are likely 
to mean that less information about corruption, misconduct and maladministration is 
reported.

notes: The Introduction provides an overall assessment. This is the Commissioner’s contemporary assessment of legislative effects, not a statement of current law. No numbered recommendations list appears.
